mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined for four consecutive weeks with an accelerating weekly drop (-19.4 to -26.3). This momentum reflects an entrenched behavioral shift away from retail and recreation trips that will persist into the next four weeks absent a reversing shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell every week from -19.4 to -26.3 over the snapshot
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days despite the four-week declining trend observed at decision time.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week PARKS drop exceeding 9 points (observed: -8.7 to -17.9) signals acute heat-driven suppression of outdoor activity, typical of a mid-July heat episode in Madrid. This suppression spills into retail and recreation trips as people curtail all discretionary outdoor movement over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -8.7 to -17.9 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not continue declining over the next two weeks even though PARKS dropped more than 9 points week-on-week at decision time.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous sustained declines in WORKPLACES (-14.1 to -22.3) and TRANSIT (-11.7 to -17.3) indicate a summer exodus of commuters and reduced use of transit-linked urban mobility infrastructure. Their joint weakening reduces incidental retail footfall tied to commuting routines, pulling RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT declined in parallel across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue to decline jointly, indicating the commuting-linkage mechanism does not hold.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has flipped from positive (+4.7) to negative (-5.9) over four weeks, consistent with residents leaving Madrid for summer vacation and reducing routine local errands. This population outflow lowers the local base of potential retail shoppers, depressing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM shifted from +4.7 to -5.9 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next four weeks despite continued negative GROCERY_PHARM readings, indicating no linkage between errand mobility and retail population base.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has stayed near zero (0.0 to -0.3) even as RETAIL_REC, PARKS, WORKPLACES and TRANSIT all fell sharply, implying people are not simply staying home but are leaving the metro area's device-location footprint altogether (e.g., traveling to second homes or coastal destinations). This net outmigration predicts continued RETAIL_REC weakness in the immediate next week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed flat near 0 while RETAIL_REC, PARKS, WORKPLACES, TRANSIT all declined
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds upward in the next week even though RESIDENTIAL remains flat and other categories keep falling, contradicting the outmigration explanation.

mechanism_narrative: If regional heat-health advisories are issued recommending reduced midday outdoor activity, this policy-driven behavioral constraint will suppress retail and recreation visits (shopping, dining, leisure) over the following two weeks, compounding the already observed PARKS and RETAIL_REC declines.
candidate_trigger: heat-health advisory issued for Community of Madrid
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell sharply to -17.9 consistent with heat-driven outdoor avoidance
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall further over two weeks even after a heat-health advisory is issued, indicating the policy trigger has no measurable retail effect.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility crossing below -15% (currently at -17.3) signals a meaningful reduction in public transport capacity usage, which mechanically limits the number of retail and recreation trips achievable in the short term, producing a near-immediate one-week drag on RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -15 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT reached -17.3 in the most recent week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week immediately following a TRANSIT reading below -15 percent, falsifying the mechanical trip-constraint link.

mechanism_narrative: The combined and accelerating declines across PARKS, WORKPLACES, and TRANSIT represent a broad-based contraction of all outside-home mobility categories, consistent with a systemic summer slowdown. When all three decline together beyond their historical pace, RETAIL_REC follows with a lagged decline over the subsequent four weeks as the same households reduce overall movement.
evidence_refs: fact:all three series declined every week across the four-week snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though PARKS, WORKPLACES, and TRANSIT all continue to jointly decline, disproving the systemic contraction linkage.
